title: Comparing Proteomic Profiles of Extracellular Vesicles from Long-term Stored Plasma Samples
author: Torres, Bernardo, et al.
materials: The aim of this study was to identify an optimal method of isolating EVs from plasma samples long-term stored in biobanks for use in investigations designed to detect new protein biomarkers.

The desalted protein digest was dried, resuspended in 10 µL of 0.1% formic acid and subjected to RP-LC-MS/MS in an Easy-nLC 1200 system coupled to an ion trap LTQ-Orbitrap-Velos-Pro hybrid mass spectrometer (Thermo Scientific). Peptides were concentrated (on-line) by reverse phase chromatography using a 0.1 mm × 20 mm C18 RP precolumn (Thermo Scientific), and then separated using a 0.075 mm x 250 mm C18 RP column (Phenomenex) operating at 0.25 µL/min. Resultant peptides were eluted using a 90-min dual gradient. The gradient profile was set as follows: 5 − 25% solvent B for 68 min, 25 − 40% solvent B for 22 min, 40 − 100% solvent B for 2 min and 100% solvent B for 18 min (Solvent A: 0.1% formic acid in water, solvent B: 0.1% formic acid, 80% ACN in water). Electrospray ionization (ESI) was performed using a nano-bore emitters Stainless Steel ID 30 μm (Proxeon) interface at 2.1 kV spray voltage with 60% S-Lens. Orbitrap resolution was set at 30,000 [27].

steps.title: Perform NTA on EV samples
steps.instruction: Characterize EV particles (UC, SEC, SEC+UC) using NanoSight NS300 with NTA 3.2 software.

substeps.instruction: Dilute SEC and SEC+UC samples 1:50 in PBS; dilute UC samples 1:100 in PBS.
Infuse each diluted sample continuously with an automatic syringe pump at 50 µL/min.
Set instrument: camera level 12, auto background subtraction/blur, minimum track length acquisition time 60 s, detection threshold 5.
Measure concentration, mean size, and size distribution; multiply reported concentrations by the respective dilution factor.

steps.title: Prepare peptide digest for RP-LC-MS/MS
steps.instruction: Resuspend dried, desalted protein digest and load onto the LC‑MS system for separation and electrospray.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend the dried digest in 10 µL of 0.1 % formic acid.
Inject the sample into an Easy-nLC 1200 system coupled to an LTQ‑Orbitrap‑Velos‑Pro hybrid mass spectrometer.
Concentrate peptides on‑line using a 0.1 mm × 20 mm C18 pre‑column (Thermo Scientific).
Separate peptides on a 0.075 mm × 250 mm C18 analytical column (Phenomenex) at a flow rate of 0.25 µL/min.

Elute with a 90‑min dual gradient: 5‑25 % solvent B for 68 min, 25‑40 % B for 22 min, 40‑100 % B for 2 min, then hold at 100 % B for 18 min. Solvent A = 0.1 % formic acid in water; Solvent B = 0.1 % formic acid, 80 % acetonitrile in water.
Perform electrospray ionization using a stainless‑steel nano‑bore emitter (ID 30 µm, Proxeon) at 2.1 kV spray voltage with 60 % S‑Lens.
Set Orbitrap resolution to 30,000.

steps.title: Run MS acquisition
steps.instruction: Acquire MS data with defined survey and data‑dependent parameters.

substeps.instruction: Collect survey scans from 400 to 1600 m/z (1 µscan).
Follow each survey scan with twenty data‑dependent MS/MS scans (Top 20).
Use an isolation width of 2 m/z and a normalized collision energy of 35 %.
Apply dynamic exclusion for 60 s intervals.
Enable charge‑state screening to reject unassigned and singly‑charged ions.

steps.title: Identify peptides with PEAKS
steps.instruction: Search raw MS data against a human protein database using PEAKS Studio XPro.

substeps.instruction: Use the UniProt‑Homo sapiens database (79,684 entries, release 06/22) with a decoy‑fusion approach.
Set enzyme specificity to semispecific tryptic cleavage after Arg and Lys, allowing up to two missed cleavages.
Apply precursor tolerance of 20 ppm and fragment tolerance of 0.6 Da.
Allow optional methionine oxidation and cysteine carbamidomethylation as variable modifications.
Restrict false discovery rates to 0.01 for both peptide‑spectrum matches and proteins.
Retain only proteins identified by at least two unique peptides.

steps.title: Functional annotation with DAVID
steps.instruction: Annotate identified EV proteins for cellular component enrichment using DAVID 2021.

substeps.instruction: Submit the protein list to DAVID 2021 for Gene Ontology cellular component analysis.
Obtain p‑values via Fisher’s exact test and apply Benjamini correction.
Consider only categories with a Benjamini‑corrected p‑value < 0.01 as strongly enriched.

steps.title: Statistical analysis in GraphPad Prism
steps.instruction: Perform statistical comparisons of EV isolation methods.

substeps.instruction: Compute descriptive statistics for each isolation method in GraphPad Prism version 9.0.
Test differences between groups using one‑way ANOVA followed by Tukey’s HSD post‑hoc test.
Report significance as * p < 0.05, ** p < 0.01, *** p < 0.001.
